source: My lord, please believe me. It was far more than a mere dream. It felt so real. I saw you bloodied, a wound in your heart.
And Hamlet was your killer.
No doubt he would be.
I suppose even those outside my own family have noticed the tension between me and my young nephew.
Perhaps I ought to speak with him, trivial dreams aside...
The time has long come due.
Well, then. That's how we know it's just a dream.
Hamlet can threaten no one any longer.
A... a... nightmare?
Killed... how?
It's hard to remember. I saw... your father, somehow—the late King, but alive, somehow—and then everyone began to die.
Y-you saw my father?
N-never mind. It doesn't matter. Leave me. I need... to be alone.
So, we all died, eh?
Maybe that would be best for us all.
To just be erased, as though we'd never existed in the first place.
And you and I turned to nothing, not even dust, just gone.
I rather like existing.
Well, that makes one of us.
Having terrible dreams? That sounds awful. I'm sorry, my dear.
Be glad it was but a dream.
I... worry that there was more truth in it than I'd have liked. It felt so real...
Nightmares often do, don't they?
You know, I've also been having... strange dreams of my own.
Of what nature, my lady?
I'm... afraid it would be inappropriate to speak of them. I... just...
I already trouble poor Irma too often as it is. I've been spending my evenings in the kitchen, as though I were a girl again...
I-if you'll excuse me, Ophelia...
I had a strange nightmare where I saw the royal court killed. But it felt... real.
My dear, I'm sorry you had a terrible dream, but fundamentally they are without consequence.
It... felt as though I'd experienced it all before. I saw Hamlet run you through with a sword!
You went to spy on him over his behavior, and—and—
Oh, no! Absolutely, absolutely not. Mad as he may be, Prince Hamlet would surely never hurt me.
Just earlier today I was speaking alone with him in the gallery. If he had ill intent, would he not have acted then?
Though... I will admit, his behavior is most peculiar. It seems random, but...
In fact, I have every intention of ensuring Hamlet causes no harm to anyone.
I intend to find him at my earliest availability. He seems to frequent the same odd places these days.
Love. Hamlet is gone.
Whatever you dreamed of him, it matters little anymore.
He shall live only in memory, now.
Are we in the business of exchanging dreams now, you and I?
It just felt so real. As though it were a memory.
Was it the sort of dream where you can control things?
I tend to have more and more of those these days. A scholar once gave me some wisdom about those.
He said that if every time you put on your shoes you think to yourself, 'Here I am, donning my shoes,' then over time, one can control one's dreams.
It's something to do with the way our memory functions.
Fascinating. Not quite what I was getting at, though.
Hmm. Perhaps the Queen could offer a sympathetic ear. Her Majesty's been suffering some nightmares herself lately.
You ge' em too?
I got one about a giant, man-eating sheep that is going to kill me.
E'ery night it closes in...
And then it bleats in m' face! BRAHH! BRAHH! An' I can't run away!
An' then I realize it's me mother!
...Not quite what I had in mind. Thank you, Marcellus.
Well, you're not the only one, 'Feely.
Gertrude's also been having trouble sleeping.
Aren't you supposed to address her as 'My Lady'?
Only when I'm on the clock, 'Feely.
Anyway, she's been sweating and saying strange things in her sleep. I think she's thinking about her dead husband. Pretty disgusting, if you ask me!
Maybe the two of you can find one another and grieve communally. I hear that can be very cathartic.
My nightmare felt real. It didn't feel like a normal dream.
Well, was I in it? Did I do anything interesting or fabulous? That's the only thing anyone cares about when you speak to them of your dreams.
...No. Your body... wasn't amongst the others. Still, I knew... that you were... already dead.
...I was... already... dead?
What a tediously boring story. Leave me be, 'Feely.
I have places to be. Things to do.
The Queen was also having trouble sleeping.
Probably should've seen it as a warning sign, in hindsight.
Gertrude had a lot of darkness in her, you know? But even despite that, she was kind to me.
Don't let the darkness overcome you.
Anyway, that's all in the past. And I don't grieve. Let's just never speak of this again.
You as well?
Have you been having nightmares, too?
No! But the Queen, she has so many.
I brought a cool cloth to her last night to calm her down. She was in such a fright.
She may be grown, but she's as much my little Gerta as ever.
She comes to visit me nearly every night, but never tells me the contents of her fitful and bloody dreams.
No! But my lady Gerta, she was having so many before she passed.
I am worried for you, my sweet.
The Queen would not want you to follow in her footsteps. Of that, I am certain.
My lord, I know for certain that Prince Fortinbras will invade very soon, violating the peace treaty.
Hah! In what world should I listen to you on matters of the state?
You know as well as I do that Lady Brit's family has been working for Norway. Who else might be?
My lord—if you would send an envoy outside the city's walls, you would see—
An envoy! The little lady's learned to use the terms of war. Fascinating.
Your father already serves my war chamber needs most excellently. I hardly need two Poloniuses fretting in my ear.
Let others handle the grand machinations. Worry less.
I... know it's difficult to believe, but I was warned by someone I trust implicitly.
Normally I'd disregard this. But your kindness to me deserves a good turn.
If this is, in some way, true...
I'd need proof of his location if I were to act.
Can your source bring me something of that nature?
I'll do my best, my lord.
I've learned that Prince Fortinbras plans to invade, violating our peace treaty.
Oh, Ophelia... while I'm sure that's entirely possible, it's above our heads.
Better leave these matters to the men who order the troops, my love. The issue is being handled.
I don't think it is. Have we considered Fortinbras might subvert—
Ophelia. I am the daughter of an Emperor. You think I haven't? But who would listen to me—or to you?
Better not to rattle my husband. He's of a fragile mind now.
I know that Prince Fortinbras is going to invade soon, violating the treaty.
And I know that you know that.
We already spoke of this.
I'll see you soon. I hope I can still trust you. I'm not great at that part. Trusting, I mean.
I won't expose you, Brit. I promise.
We have to stop him.
Even if that were true, what on earth makes you think I can do something about it?
Is there something you want to say to me? Spit it out, or stop wasting my time.
Father, I know for certain that Lord Fortinbras is going to invade, violating the peace treaty.
Of course you do. You're my clever child. I wasn't certain you'd noticed... but I cannot say I am surprised.
The way the King refuses to listen to me! To any of his advisors—Bernardo included!
Both Bernardo and I have been trying to convince my lord for weeks that a coup was on our doorstep. But he won't listen.
Even after Lady Brit was outed as a spy within our own walls, for God's sake!
He's too wrapped up in trying to please the Danish nobility, in making shows of force, in asserting his power...
His desire for acknowledgement has left him blind to the tenuous position we're in.
King Hamlet would never have misjudged so greatly for so long.
Father, if you and I both know Fortinbras will come for us, can't we do something about it?
...Not without proof.
Had we any concrete evidence to show that Fortinbras is lying about his plans to invade the Polacks, we might succeed at convincing Claudius.
Now that her allegiances have been exposed, if Bernardo could extract anything from Lady Brit... we might have a chance.
But I'm uncertain whether she'll be willing to talk to him at all.
But to do that, we'd need to know someone connected to Norway—and we haven't anyone like that in Elsinore.
...Maybe we do.
Oho. Is Claudius's paranoia about spies and treason rubbing off on you?
Careful about that, love.
Both Bernardo and I had been trying to convince the King for weeks that a coup was on our doorstep. But he wouldn't listen, up until the end.
Had we any concrete evidence to show that Fortinbras is lying about his plans to invade the Polacks, we might of succeeded at convincing Claudius.
I know for certain that Lord Fortinbras is going to invade, violating the peace treaty.
(I'm a little early, I suppose. He hasn't heard anything about this yet.)
Never mind. It'll make sense later, perhaps.
Step outside and enjoy the sunlight a little more. Don't go the way of Hamlet. I need at least one sane friend.
Ophelia. It's as if you're trying to have me deposed from my post.
You're correct that we all suspect Prince Fortinbras is subverting his uncle's wishes.
Still, without compelling evidence that Fortinbras has violated his agreement not to enter Denmark...
We have nothing.
Have you found some trusted witness willing to confess everything they know?
Hmm. Perhaps.
Let us hear it then, if you have such compelling evidence.
Until then, step outside and enjoy the sunlight a little more. Don't go the way of Hamlet. I need at least one sane friend.
N... no. Not yet.
But I will.
All right. All right, Ophelia.
Fortinbras has told the King he intends to pass through Denmark on his way to attack Poland, right?
Isn't there a distinct possibility he's lying to us and intends to take Elsinore? After all, his father was killed by King Hamlet...
Y...yes. There is that possibility. But Ophelia, we live in a time of constant war. That's always a possibility.
Right now, Denmark needs allies, and Fortinbras is offering us that chance. Unless there's some compelling evidence to show otherwise, we must trust him.
I know for a fact that Prince Fortinbras is going to stage an invasion.
